key_insight: LLM agents can turn natural-language home energy preferences into reliable appliance schedules, reaching near-MILP performance when connected to live pricing, weather, and device data.
engineering_relevance: This work suggests a practical control interface for residential demand response and solar-aware scheduling, helping reduce electricity costs without requiring users to write optimization constraints.
method: Built a tool-calling ReAct agent for multi-appliance scheduling.
Integrated live Octopus Agile prices, weather forecasts, PV estimates, usage data, and a retrieval-augmented knowledge base.
Benchmarked GPT-4o-mini, Gemini 2.5 Flash, and Claude Sonnet 4.6 against MILP ground truth across tariff, conflict, and week-long scenarios.
evidence_signal: In evaluation, native function calling achieved 100% scheduling success and 96.7–98.0% of oracle savings over a simulated week, with roughly GBP 1,270 annual savings projected versus an off-peak timer baseline.
watch_item: Results depend on reliable tool calling and accurate external inputs; text-parsed action interfaces were notably less dependable, and real-world deployment must handle forecast and data errors.
paper_title: LLMs for Agentic Home Energy Management
